To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the out-of-sample errors of ML models for molecular properties are smaller than the DFT error and are on par with or close to chemical accuracy for most properties.

(1) the best ML models of electronic ground state molecular properties are obtained with GC and GG regressors and MG or HDAD representations, (2) ML models are more accurate than hybrid density functional theory for all properties and (3) the errors of the ML models are smaller than the errors of the hybrid DFT reference.

(1) ML models can be trained to predict 13 electronic ground-state properties of organic molecules to within chemical accuracy; (2) the performance of ML models is strongly dependent on the representation of molecules and the choice of regressor; (3) the performance of hybrid DFT (B 3 LYP/6-31G(d,p)) is not competitive with the best ML models, and (4) the prediction errors of the best performing ML models are less than hybrid DFT errors
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of fast, accurate, and reliable ML models of molecular properties.

developing and evaluating ML models for the accurate prediction of electronic properties of organic molecules, which are of importance in the context of drug discovery, materials design and chemical reaction prediction.
developing fast ML models for the prediction of ground state electronic and energetic properties of organic molecules with out of sample errors close to chemical accuracy.

ML models can achieve chemical accuracy and that they can be more accurate than DFT if explicitly correlated quantum data were available.
ML models can be made to perform as well as hybrid DFT, or better, if appropriate molecular representations are selected for the specific property to be predicted.
